key_insight: A neural network potential trained on first-principles data can accurately reproduce oxygen-vacancy energetics and enable long-timescale diffusion simulations in SrTiO3.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to predict defect transport in perovskite oxides with near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the cost, aiding materials design for electronic and ionic functionality.
method: Trained an NNP on AIMD/DFT reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Validated energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes.
Used large-scale NNP-MD and Arrhenius analysis to extract vacancy diffusion coefficients and migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP matched DFT reference properties and produced a vacancy migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV, close to the experimental 0.67 eV.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the DFT training set, so unusual defect states or compositions outside the sampled space may require retraining.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
